newsitem.title: THAILAND: Further Thai economic downturns unlikely - Paribas.
newsitem.headline: Further Thai economic downturns unlikely - Paribas.

text.p: Paribas Capital Markets said on Thursday that the Thai economy appears to have stabilised and further downturns were unlikely.
A slowdown in manufacturing production had eased and private investment had stabilised, it said.
"In fact, the economic situation appears to have stabilised and no further deterioration is seen on several fronts," the Singapore-based firm said in a new report.
Paribas said the country's exports were expected to remain sluggish in the next quarter, but an upturn was possible in the second quarter of 1997.
"There appears to be some early signs of a bottoming-out of private investment. A sustained pick-up will result in a rise in production and eventually exports," it said.
There could also be reforms in Thailand's foreign exchange policy next year after the economy rebounded, Paribas said.
The baht's value is fixed daily by the central bank against a basket of currencies heavily weighted in the U.S. dollar.
The baht is now only allowed to move within a four-satang band, two satangs on either side of the daily fix, by the central bank.
"Given that a widening of the band is more a stop-gap measure, we think that a new trade-weighted exchange rate basket is more likely," it said.
The weights for the yen, European and regional currencies might be raised at the expense of the U.S. dollar, it said.
